key_insight: Near-teacher performance on supervised distributions can mask incomplete capability transfer and out-of-distribution forgetting after on-policy distillation.
engineering_relevance: Teams consolidating specialized models should test extrapolative and compositional generalization rather than relying on in-distribution scores alone.
method: Evaluate single- and multi-teacher on-policy distillation on synthetic reasoning and Qwen3-based tasks.
Probe teacher capability, data coverage, and update geometry as explanations for generalization gaps.
Propose geometry-based patching and base-preserving replay to improve OOD retention.
evidence_signal: Across math, coding, agent, and long-context evaluations, extrapolative IND scores reached 96.04–102.73% of teacher scores, while OOD scores remained 2.45–16.25% below the base model; compositional OOD scores were 18.19–24.34% below the best teachers.
watch_item: Eliminating OOD forgetting by jointly improving teacher capability and data coverage was demonstrated only in the reported experiments, not as a general guarantee.
paper_title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
